A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework. Their main sections, equations, experimental displays, and Appendices A–D are readable and can be matched despite revisions and pagination changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original stylized simulations and Fashion-MNIST federated experiments in Section 7, with additional robustness findings in Appendix D.3.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds audit-estimation, noise, metric-alignment, and FEMNIST attack–defense experiments in Tables 5–8.

M1.justification: The proposed Eval–Info–Reward–Audit framework, mixed challenges, greedy audit selection, and hysteresis-based switching procedures are retained. Expanded mathematical formalization and additional experimental conditions do not establish a changed proposed training or governance algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 retains the stylized and Fashion-MNIST evaluations and adds FEMNIST, with digits as head classes and letters as tail classes. It also evaluates noisy-update environments and model-poisoning/backdoor threat scenarios beyond v2's head-focused gaming.

E2.justification: Table 8 newly compares FedCC and Attack-Adaptive Aggregation under no attack, PoisonedFL-style poisoning, and backdoor/model-replacement attacks. These evaluated defenses and attack variants were absent from v2's aligned-versus-gaming comparisons.

E3.justification: The original 30-client, 40-round Fashion-MNIST experiment is retained. Additional experiments introduce partial-audit sampling at fractions 0.10/0.25/0.50 with threshold 0.05, clipped Gaussian updates, mixed head/tail metrics, and client-side tail-welfare evaluation. FEMNIST uses 32 clients, 12 participants per round, 100 rounds, and same-defense PoG references.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained sanction/disclosure sweeps and Appendix D.3 checks, Tables 5–8 test whether partial audits recover risk rankings and threshold decisions, how noise and metric alignment affect welfare separation, and whether the diagnostic patterns persist under contemporary attacks and defenses.

E5.justification: v2 mentions averaging across seeds without quantified uncertainty. v3 Table 5 reports standard deviations of PoG estimates across audit-resampling trials, averaged over six gaming profiles. The trial count is unspecified; this does not establish an increase in FL training runs.

E6.justification: The original baseline tables are unchanged, but Tables 5–8 add substantial results. Audit-estimate standard deviation decreases from 0.0222 to 0.0060 with greater coverage; Table 7's paired PoG decreases from 0.0585 to 0.0329 with increased alignment. Table 8 reports PoisonedFL-style PoG of 0.3623 under FedCC and −0.3154 under Attack-Adaptive Aggregation, each relative to its own defense baseline.

T1.justification: Proposition 5.4 and Appendix A.2 correct the participation map from 1−FΘ(ΔU) to FΘ(ΔU). Section 4.5 adds baseline-relative rationality definitions, compactness and penalty-separability assumptions, and revised threshold arguments. Resilience is generalized to 1−L(π), and Appendix A.1 substantially rewrites the manipulability–PoG derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about the three-layer framework, gaming/cooperation indices, participation thresholds, and governance toolkit. Additional validation does not redefine those core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 8 adds substantive interpretations of negative PoG, reference and defense dependence, estimator reliability, threshold errors, and robustness across noise/alignment regimes. The privacy limitation changes from no explicit privacy simulation to DP-like perturbations without full privacy accounting. The broader-impact discussion adds concrete miscalibration and enforcement safeguards.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement changes from two anonymous notebooks plus README instructions to one notebook covering all experiments and an announced public repository. v3 also supplies perturbation formulas and concrete FEMNIST optimization settings. The original Appendix D implementation description remains largely unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 is unchanged, but Sections 3 and 5–6 add explicit positioning against generic principal–agent abstractions and explain the FL-specific role of otherwise standard mathematical ingredients. The new full Nemhauser et al. reference completes an attribution already present in v2 Appendix A.3.

P1.justification: Sections 3, 4.5, 5.1–5.2, and 6 undergo extensive rewriting, including recurring explanations of FL relevance, assumptions, and technical challenges. Discussion and limitations are reorganized into numerous named subsections, and the broader-impact and reproducibility passages are rewritten.

P2.justification: v2's two multi-panel bar-chart figures become v3 Tables 2–3, preserving the sweep analyses in tabular form. The original Fashion-MNIST table becomes Table 4, and four new result tables are added, including a grouped defense comparison. This substantially changes the experimental presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful tests of estimator reliability and robustness beyond v2's illustrative validation, and corrects the reversed participation CDF. The gain is limited: the expanded Proposition 4.17 proof still does not justify finite, ordered thresholds, and new Table 6 reports PoG=0.0545 where its stated baseline implies approximately 0.0614. These theoretical and reporting issues temper the benefit of the broader evidence.
